name: Equatorial Guinea

intro: Equatorial Guinea includes a mainland **continente** (continental region) and islands in the Gulf of Guinea. Spanish is an official language, alongside other languages spoken across its communities.
fun_fact: Bioko is an **isla** (island) in the Gulf of Guinea; Malabo, the capital, is on its northern coast.

regions.famous_place: Pico Basilé and the southern highlands

cultura.name: Mvet storytelling
cultura.description:
The **Fang** (a major cultural group) preserve oral histories through performance.
The **mvet** (harp-like instrument and epic tradition) accompanies songs and stories.
cultura.credit: Tradición Oral y Comunidad · CC BY-SA 4.0

cultura.name: Balélé dance
cultura.description:
The **Bubi** (Bioko's Indigenous people) preserve dance and percussion traditions.
The **balélé** (traditional dance) is performed at community occasions.

cultura.name: Many languages, one country
cultura.description:
Spanish is an official language, alongside French and Portuguese.
Fang, Bubi, and other local languages also matter in daily life; **idioma** means language.

cultura.name: Cultural exchange
cultura.description:
Community displays share food, music, and national symbols with new audiences.
This image records an Equatorial Guinea booth at an international university culture festival.

india_traveller.visa_note: A **visado** (visa) is required for many visitors, but the rules and application route for Indian ordinary-passport holders must be confirmed with the Equatorial Guinea mission responsible for India. Also verify passport validity, health documentation, and current border procedures before booking.
india_traveller.visa_application_note: Confirm with the mission serving India
india_traveller.flight_note: Compare live routes to Malabo (SSG) or Bata (BSG) from major Indian airports. Allow for multiple connections and verify transit visas, operating days, and onward transport before purchase; check **carretera** (road) conditions for onward travel.
india_traveller.cost_reference_note: No comparable, reproducible INR cost source was verified; no estimate supplied.
india_traveller.veg_tips: Meals often include fish, meat, or palm oil; ask about ingredients and cooking stock. A simple **yuca** (cassava) or **plátano** (plantain) side may be available, but confirm it was not cooked with meat.
india_traveller.key_food_phrase: Sin carne ni pescado, por favor

verification_notes: The cited UK FCDO page is written for British passport holders and is not Indian visa advice; verify every entry and health requirement with Equatorial Guinea's authorities.
No source was found to support the former INR daily-cost estimate or a specific India-to-Equatorial Guinea route, duration, or carriers; those values were left null.

research_reflection: Equatorial Guinea's island and mainland settings, Spanish-language heritage, and distinct community traditions are often overlooked in broad regional summaries. A careful **idioma** (language) and culture guide should reflect that diversity without treating any one community as representative of all.
